# Brisa

> Brisa is a zero-dependency Go micro-framework for building desktop applications with an HTML/CSS/JS frontend and a Go backend. The Go side registers typed IPC commands (REPR pattern: Request → Endpoint → Response); the frontend calls them through an auto-injected JavaScript SDK (`window.brisa`). Brisa ships 6 optional built-in desktop CSS themes, or you can disable them and bring your own CSS.

Module path: `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa` (Go 1.26+, standard library only).
Import it as `brisa`. All public types are re-exported from the root package; never import `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa/core` in application code.

This document is written for LLMs and coding agents. Every API listed here exists in the source code. Do not invent APIs that are not listed.

---

## 1. How Brisa works (mental model)

1. `brisa.New(cfg)` creates an `*App`.
2. You register commands with `brisa.Bind(...)`, `brisa.BindService(...)` or `brisa.BindEndpoint(...)`.
3. `app.Run()` starts a loopback HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:<random port>`, opens a desktop window pointing at it, and blocks until the window closes or SIGINT/SIGTERM arrives.
4. When the server serves `index.html`, it auto-injects into `<head>` (unless `/brisa/sdk.js` is already present in the HTML):
   - `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">`
   - `<link rel="manifest" href="/brisa/manifest.json">`
   - `<link rel="icon" ... href="/brisa/icon.png">` + `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/brisa/icon.png">` (if `Config.Icon` resolves and HTML has no `rel="icon"`)
   - `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/brisa/theme.css">` (unless `DisableThemeCSS: true` or HTML already links a `/brisa/*.css` theme)
   - `<script src="/brisa/sdk.js"></script>`
5. In the browser, `window.brisa.call.<namespace>.<name>(payload)` sends a POST to `/brisa/rpc` with a per-session token, Go binds + validates the JSON into your request struct, runs the handler, and returns the response as JSON.
6. Go → UI push events go over Server-Sent Events (`app.Emit` → `brisa.on` in JS).

Window backends:
- macOS with cgo enabled: native `NSWindow` + `WKWebView`.
- Everything else (Linux, Windows, or `CGO_ENABLED=0`): an installed Chromium/Chrome/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi in `--app=` mode, controlled over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`brisa.LocateBrowser()` returns the auto-detected binary path). Set `WindowConfig.BrowserPath` to force a specific binary.
- `WindowConfig.Headless: true`: no window; the server keeps running until SIGINT/SIGTERM (useful for tests/CI or opening the URL in a normal browser).

---

## 2. Minimal project layout

```text
myapp/
├── go.mod
├── main.go
└── ui/
    ├── index.html
    └── (optional) icon.png, style.css, app.js, images...
```

The frontend is embedded with `embed.FS`. `AssetsSubDir: "ui"` makes `ui/index.html` be served at `/`.
Unknown paths without a matching file fall back to `index.html` (SPA-friendly).

---

## 3. Minimal app (using a built-in theme)

`main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"log"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa"
)

//go:embed ui
var uiAssets embed.FS

type GreetRequest struct {
	Name string `json:"name" doc:"Person to greet" example:"Ada" validate:"required,min=2,max=40"`
}

type GreetResponse struct {
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

func main() {
	app := brisa.New(brisa.Config{
		AppID:        "com.example.hello",
		Title:        "Hello Brisa",
		Theme:        brisa.ThemeAdwaita,
		Assets:       uiAssets,
		AssetsSubDir: "ui",
		Window: brisa.WindowConfig{
			Width:  900,
			Height: 600,
		},
	})

	app.Use(brisa.Recover(), brisa.Logger())

	brisa.Bind(app, "greet", func(ctx *brisa.Context, req GreetRequest) (GreetResponse, error) {
		return GreetResponse{Message: "Hello, " + req.Name + "!"}, nil
	}).Summary("Greets a person")

	log.Fatal(app.Run())
}
```

`ui/index.html` (do NOT add `<script src="/brisa/sdk.js">` or the theme `<link>` yourself — they are injected):

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <title>Hello Brisa</title>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="adw-split-view" style="grid-template-columns: 1fr;">
    <section class="adw-content-view">
      <header class="adw-toolbar"><strong>Hello Brisa</strong></header>
      <main class="adw-page">
        <div class="adw-clamp">
          <div class="boxed-list">
            <div class="adw-row">
              <div class="adw-row-text">
                <input id="name" class="adw-entry-input" placeholder="Your name" />
              </div>
              <div class="adw-row-suffix">
                <button class="gtk-btn suggested-action" onclick="greet()">Greet</button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <p id="out"></p>
        </div>
      </main>
    </section>
  </div>

  <script>
    async function greet() {
      try {
        const res = await brisa.call.greet({ name: document.getElementById("name").value });
        document.getElementById("out").textContent = res.message;
      } catch (err) {
        // err is a brisa.BrisaError
        document.getElementById("out").textContent =
          err.errors ? Object.values(err.errors).flat().join(", ") : err.message;
      }
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

Run: `go run .`

---

## 4. `brisa.Config` reference

```go
brisa.Config{
	AppID:              "com.example.app",  // default "com.brisa.app"; also used for the store directory
	Title:              "My App",           // default "Brisa Desktop App"
	Version:            "1.0.0",            // default "1.0.0"
	Description:        "…",                // shown in schema/inspector
	Icon:               "assets/icon.png",  // looked up in Assets (raw and sub dir), then on disk; include it in //go:embed (e.g. //go:embed ui assets/icon.png or put icon.png inside ui/) so packaged binaries find it; served at /brisa/icon.png
	Addr:               "127.0.0.1:0",      // default; random loopback port
	Assets:             uiAssets,           // fs.FS (usually embed.FS)
	AssetsSubDir:       "ui",               // sub-directory inside Assets used as web root
	IndexHTML:          "",                 // inline HTML used when no Assets file matches
	DevServerURL:       "",                 // e.g. "http://localhost:5173" to reverse-proxy a Vite dev server
	InspectorURL:       "/brisa/inspector", // default; set "-" to disable the IPC Inspector
	Theme:              brisa.ThemeAdwaita, // built-in CSS theme (default Adwaita)
	DisableThemeCSS:    false,              // true = no built-in theme CSS at all (bring your own)
	DisableCSRFToken:   false,              // true disables token + host checks (NOT recommended)
	SilenceTagWarnings: false,              // silence startup warnings about required on zero-rejecting primitives (also brisa.SilenceTagWarnings(true))
	Window:             brisa.WindowConfig{ /* see below */ },
	Store:              brisa.StoreOptions{ /* see section 10 */ },
}
```

`brisa.WindowConfig`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Title` | Window title (defaults to `Config.Title`) |
| `Width`, `Height` | Initial size (defaults 1080×720) |
| `MinWidth`, `MinHeight` | Minimum size (defaults 680×480; negative = no minimum) |
| `X`, `Y` | Initial position |
| `Center` | Center on screen |
| `Fullscreen`, `Maximized` | Initial state |
| `Frameless` | No native title bar |
| `AlwaysOnTop` | Keep above other windows |
| `Headless` | Do not open a window |
| `BrowserPath` | Force a Chromium binary (Chromium backend) |
| `CustomFlags` | Extra Chromium flags (Chromium backend) |

---

## 5. Registering commands (Go side)

### 5.1 `brisa.Bind` — typed function handler (preferred)

```go
func Bind[TReq any, TRes any](r CommandRegistrar, name string,
	handler func(ctx *brisa.Context, req TReq) (TRes, error)) *brisa.Command
```

- `r` is `*brisa.App` or `*brisa.CommandGroup`.
- The JSON payload is decoded into `TReq`, then validated (section 6). Invalid payload → error.
- Use `brisa.Empty` (or `struct{}`) for "no input" or "no output". An empty response type replies with `null`.
- `brisa.Map` (`map[string]any`) is handy for ad-hoc responses.

```go
brisa.Bind(app, "ping", func(ctx *brisa.Context, _ brisa.Empty) (brisa.Map, error) {
	return brisa.Map{"pong": true}, nil
})
```

### 5.2 Command metadata (fluent, builder methods return `*Command`)

```go
cmd := brisa.Bind(app, "tasks.create", handler).
	Summary("Create a task").
	Description("Longer description for the inspector").
	Tags("Tasks").
	Deprecated().
	Middleware(brisa.Timeout(5 * time.Second))

doc := cmd.Doc() // brisa.CommandDoc
```

### 5.3 Groups / namespaces

Command names are dot-separated. Groups prefix names and can carry middleware and tags.

```go
tasks := app.Group("tasks").Tags("Tasks")         // also: app.Group("tasks", mw1, mw2)
brisa.Bind(tasks, "list", listHandler)            // command "tasks.list"
brisa.Bind(tasks, "create", createHandler)        // command "tasks.create"

admin := tasks.Group("admin", requireAdmin)       // command prefix "tasks.admin"
admin.Use(brisa.RateLimiter(brisa.RateLimiterOptions{Max: 10, Window: time.Minute}))
```

In JS these become `brisa.call.tasks.list()`, `brisa.call.tasks.create({...})`, `brisa.call.tasks.admin.xxx()`.

### 5.4 `brisa.BindService` — expose all methods of a struct

```go
type SystemService struct{}

func (s *SystemService) Info() (SystemInfo, error) { … }                       // system.info
func (s *SystemService) Echo(req EchoReq) (EchoRes, error) { … }               // system.echo
func (s *SystemService) Whoami(ctx *brisa.Context) (brisa.Map, error) { … }    // system.whoami
func (s *SystemService) Save(ctx *brisa.Context, req SaveReq) (brisa.Empty, error) { … }

cmds := brisa.BindService(app, "system", &SystemService{}) // returns []*brisa.Command
```

- Command name = `namespace + "." + methodName with first letter lower-cased` (if `namespace == ""`, registers `<camelCaseMethodName>` at root).
- Supported signatures: `func() (R, error)`, `func(Req) (R, error)`, `func(*brisa.Context) (R, error)`, `func(*brisa.Context, Req) (R, error)` (`Req` can be a value or `*Req` pointer). Other exported methods are silently skipped.

### 5.5 `brisa.BindEndpoint` — struct implementing `Handle`

```go
type CreateTask struct{ /* dependencies */ }

func (e *CreateTask) Handle(ctx *brisa.Context, req CreateTaskRequest) (Task, error) { … }

brisa.BindEndpoint(app, "tasks.create", &CreateTask{})
```

### 5.6 Returning errors

```go
err := brisa.NewError(404, "TASK_NOT_FOUND", "task does not exist")
err.Details = brisa.Map{"id": req.ID} // optional; err.Errors (map[string][]string) is also supported
return Task{}, err
```

- `*brisa.RPCError` → its `Status`, `Code`, `Message`, `Details` and `Errors` are forwarded to the UI.
- Validation errors → status 422, code `VALIDATION_FAILED`, with `errors: {field: [messages]}`.
- Any other Go `error` → status 500, code `INTERNAL_ERROR`, message = `err.Error()`.
- Unknown command → 404 `COMMAND_NOT_FOUND`. Malformed JSON → 400 `INVALID_PAYLOAD`.

### 5.7 `*brisa.Context` API (inside handlers and middleware)

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Context() context.Context` / `WithContext(ctx)` | Standard context (cancellation, deadlines) |
| `App() *brisa.App` | Parent app |
| `Command() string`, `RequestID() string`, `SetRequestID(id)` | Invocation info |
| `RawPayload() json.RawMessage`, `BindJSON(dest) error` | Raw input access |
| `Set(k, v)`, `Get(k) (any, bool)`, `MustGet(k) any` | Request-scoped values (e.g. set by middleware) |
| `Next() error` | Continue the middleware chain |
| `Status(code) *brisa.Context`, `Reply(status, data) error`, `Error(status, code, msg) error` | Low-level reply helpers |
| `Result() (data any, status int, replied bool)` | Inspect recorded response (e.g. in post-handler middleware) |
| `Emit(event, data)` | Push an event to the UI |
| `Window()`, `Dialog()`, `Clipboard()`, `Store()` | Native controllers |
| `Notify(brisa.NotificationOptions) error` | Desktop notification |

---

## 6. Validation and schema tags

Tags on request struct fields:

| Tag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `json:"name"` | Wire name (also used as the key in validation `errors`) |
| `validate:"..."` | Comma-separated rules |
| `msg:"..."` (or `message:"..."`) | Custom messages: `"required:Name is required\|min:{field} is too short"`, or a single message for all rules (`{field}` interpolates the field name). Panics at `Bind` time if used without `validate` or referencing a rule not in `validate`. |
| `brisa:"nowarn"` | Silences zero-value `required` startup warnings on this field |
| `doc:"..."` | Field description (Inspector + TypeScript docs) |
| `example:"..."` | Example value (Inspector pre-fills it) |

Supported rules (anything else panics at `Bind` time):

| Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `required` | Non-zero value; strings must be non-blank; slices/maps non-empty; pointers non-nil |
| `min=N`, `max=N` | Strings: rune length; numbers: value; slices/arrays/maps: item count (does NOT skip `""`; use `*string` when optional) |
| `len=N` | Exact length for strings, slices, arrays, maps (does NOT skip `""`; use `*string` when optional) |
| `oneof=a,b,c` | Value must match one option (comma- or space-separated `oneof=a b c`; empty string `""` is skipped unless `required`) |
| `email`, `url`, `uuid` | Format checks (empty string `""` is skipped unless `required`) |
| `omitempty`, `nowarn` | Accepted no-ops (`omitempty` does NOT skip following rules on empty values; `nowarn` silences tag warnings) |

Important validation behaviors:
- **Optional strings with `min` or `len`:** do NOT write `string` with `validate:"omitempty,min=3"` — `omitempty` is a no-op and `""` has length `0 < 3`. Use a pointer `*string` (`nil` pointers skip all rules except `required`).
- **`required` on `bool` and numbers (`int*`, `uint*`, `float*`):** non-pointer primitives reject Go zero values (`false` and `0`) and log a `[BRISA WARNING]` at startup. Use `*bool` / `*int` if `false` or `0` are valid inputs, or silence the warning with `brisa:"nowarn"`, `validate:"required,nowarn"`, `Config.SilenceTagWarnings: true`, or `brisa.SilenceTagWarnings(true)`.
- Nested structs, pointers, slices of structs and embedded structs are validated recursively (slice errors use keys like `"items[0].title"`).

Custom validation: implement `brisa.Validator` and/or `brisa.ContextValidator` (value or pointer receiver; if both are implemented, both run). Root struct errors are reported under `"_general"`; nested struct validator errors are reported under the nested field's path (e.g. `"address"`).

```go
func (r *CreateTaskRequest) Validate() error { … }                  // brisa.Validator
func (r *CreateTaskRequest) Validate(ctx *brisa.Context) error { … } // brisa.ContextValidator
```

---

## 7. Middleware

A middleware is `func(ctx *brisa.Context) error`. Call `ctx.Next()` to continue; return an error to abort.

```go
func requireAdmin(ctx *brisa.Context) error {
	if !isAdmin() {
		return brisa.NewError(403, "FORBIDDEN", "admin only")
	}
	return ctx.Next()
}
```

Order: global (`app.Use`) → group (`Group(..., mw)` / `group.Use`) → per-command (`.Middleware(...)`) → handler.

Built-ins:

```go
app.Use(
	brisa.Recover(),                                                           // panic → 500 INTERNAL_PANIC
	brisa.Logger(),                                                            // standard log package
	brisa.SlogLogger(),                                                        // JSON slog on stdout, or pass brisa.SlogLoggerOptions{Logger: l}
	brisa.RequestID(),                                                         // ensures req_<hex>, or pass brisa.RequestIDOptions{Generator: fn}
	brisa.Timeout(10*time.Second),                                             // deadline exceeded → 408 COMMAND_TIMEOUT (check <-ctx.Context().Done())
	brisa.RateLimiter(brisa.RateLimiterOptions{Max: 100, Window: time.Minute}), // exceeded → 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (per-command; defaults 60/1m)
)
```

---

## 8. Events (Go ⇄ UI)

Go:

```go
app.Emit("download:progress", brisa.Map{"percent": 42})   // to all windows + Go subscribers
ctx.Emit("tasks:created", task)                           // same, from a handler
app.On("ui:ready", func(data any) { … })                  // exact event name only (no "*" wildcard or unsubscribe in Go)
```

JS:

```js
const off = brisa.on("download:progress", (data) => console.log(data.percent));
brisa.once("tasks:created", (task) => …);
brisa.on("*", ({ event, data }) => …);   // wildcard (JS only)
await brisa.emit("ui:ready", { at: Date.now() });   // reaches app.On handlers and other listeners
off(); // unsubscribe
```

Typical background pusher (from the example app):

```go
app.OnReady(func(a *brisa.App) {
	go func() {
		t := time.NewTicker(time.Second)
		defer t.Stop()
		for {
			select {
			case <-a.Window().Done():
				return
			case <-t.C:
				a.Emit("system:telemetry", brisa.Map{"goroutines": runtime.NumGoroutine()})
			}
		}
	}()
})
```

---

## 9. JavaScript SDK (`window.brisa`)

Injected automatically. Available globally as `brisa`. Every command, window, dialog, clipboard, store, notify and openExternal helper is **async** (returns a `Promise`).

```js
brisa.appId; brisa.title; brisa.theme;      // theme = active built-in theme name
brisa.schemas;                              // command schemas (same as /brisa/schema.json commands)

await brisa.call.tasks.create({ title: "x", priority: "high" });  // namespaced proxy
await brisa.invoke("tasks.create", { … });                         // by name
await brisa.commands["tasks.create"]({ … });                      // flat map
await brisa.batch([{ command: "a", payload: {} }, { command: "b", payload: {} }]); // returns array of {status,data?,error?,requestId}

// Errors
try { … } catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof brisa.BrisaError) { e.code; e.status; e.message; e.errors; e.details; e.command; e.requestId; }
}

// Window (all return Promises)
await brisa.window.setTitle(t); await brisa.window.setSize(w, h); await brisa.window.setMinSize(w, h);
await brisa.window.setPosition(x, y); await brisa.window.minimize(); await brisa.window.maximize();
await brisa.window.restore(); await brisa.window.setFullscreen(true); await brisa.window.close();
const win = await brisa.window.state();  // { title, width, height, x, y, state }

// Dialogs (native OS, all return Promises)
await brisa.dialog.info(title, msg); await brisa.dialog.warn(title, msg); await brisa.dialog.error(title, msg);
const { confirmed } = await brisa.dialog.confirm(title, msg);
const { path }      = await brisa.dialog.openFile({ title, defaultPath, filters: [{ name: "Images", patterns: ["*.png"] }] });
const { paths }     = await brisa.dialog.openMultipleFiles(opts);
const { path: dir } = await brisa.dialog.openDirectory(opts);
const { path: out } = await brisa.dialog.saveFile({ defaultName: "report.txt" });

// Clipboard
await brisa.clipboard.writeText("hi");
const { text } = await brisa.clipboard.readText();

// Persistent store (note return shapes!)
await brisa.store.set("prefs", { compact: true });
const { key, value, exists } = await brisa.store.get("prefs");
const { keys } = await brisa.store.keys();   // wrapped object: { keys: string[] }
const allMap   = await brisa.store.all();    // plain key/value object: { [k: string]: any }
await brisa.store.delete("prefs");
await brisa.store.clear();

// Misc
await brisa.notify({ title: "Done", body: "Export finished", subtitle: "optional", icon: "", urgency: "normal" });
await brisa.openExternal("https://example.com");
```

TypeScript declarations are generated at `/brisa/types.d.ts` (`BrisaCommandMap` + `window.brisa` with typed `invoke`, `on`, `once`, `emit`, `appId`, `title`). In TypeScript projects, call `brisa.invoke("tasks.create", payload)` for out-of-the-box type checking, or augment `BrisaSDK` if using `brisa.call.*` / native namespaces.

---

## 10. Native features from Go

```go
// Window
w := app.Window()
w.SetTitle("…"); w.SetSize(1200, 800); w.SetMinSize(800, 600); w.SetPosition(10, 10)
w.Minimize(); w.Maximize(); w.Restore(); w.SetFullscreen(true); w.Close()
w.Title(); w.Size(); w.Position(); w.State()   // brisa.WindowStateNormal | Minimized | Maximized | Fullscreen
w.Eval("window.onNativePing && window.onNativePing()") // returns (value, err) on Chromium/CDP only; on macOS WKWebView & SSE fallback runs async and returns (nil, nil)
<-w.Done()                                     // closed channel when window closes

// Dialogs
d := app.Dialog()
d.Info(title, msg); d.Warn(title, msg); d.Error(title, msg)
d.Message(brisa.MessageDialogOptions{Title: "…", Message: "…", Kind: "info"}) // info|warning|error|question (emits "brisa:dialog:message" if no OS dialog tool exists)
ok, _ := d.Confirm("Delete?", "This cannot be undone")
path, _ := d.OpenFile(brisa.FileDialogOptions{Filters: []brisa.FileFilter{{Name: "Text", Patterns: []string{"*.txt"}}}})
paths, _ := d.OpenMultipleFiles(brisa.FileDialogOptions{})
dir, _ := d.OpenDirectory(brisa.FileDialogOptions{})
save, _ := d.SaveFile(brisa.FileDialogOptions{DefaultName: "out.txt"})
// Note: FileDialogOptions.Filters and DefaultName apply on Linux (zenity); macOS osascript openMultipleFiles selects a single file.

// Clipboard
app.Clipboard().WriteText("hi"); text, _ := app.Clipboard().ReadText()

// Notifications (native OS notification; on macOS cgo uses Config.Icon automatically; suppressed in Headless mode; also emits "brisa:notification" to UI)
app.Notify(brisa.NotificationOptions{Title: "Hi", Body: "…", Subtitle: "", Icon: "", Urgency: "normal"})

// Open URL / file in default app, or locate Chromium browser
brisa.OpenExternal("https://example.com")
browserBin := brisa.LocateBrowser()
```

### Store (persistent key/value + JSON)

File: `os.UserConfigDir()/<AppID>/store.json`. Optional AES-256-GCM encryption at rest.

```go
brisa.Config{
	Store: brisa.StoreOptions{
		EncryptionKey: "any passphrase",   // enables encryption
		Path:          "",                // override file path
		MemoryOnly:    false,             // RAM only (tests)
	},
}

s := ctx.Store() // or app.Store()
_ = s.Set("tasks", items)
var items []Task
found, err := s.Get("tasks", &items)
s.GetString("name", "default"); s.GetInt("count", 0); s.GetBool("flag", false) // fallback arg is optional
s.GetAny("k"); s.Has("k"); s.Delete("k"); s.Clear(); s.Keys(); s.All(); s.Path()
```

---

## 11. Lifecycle hooks & App methods

```go
app.OnStartup(func(ctx context.Context) error { return nil }) // before server/window; error aborts Run
app.OnReady(func(a *brisa.App) { log.Println(a.BaseURL()) })   // after the window launches
app.OnBeforeClose(func(a *brisa.App) bool { return true })     // return false to cancel shutdown
app.OnShutdown(func(a *brisa.App) { /* cleanup */ })
```

All four `On*` methods and `app.Use(...)` return `*brisa.App` (chainable).

Other `*brisa.App` methods:
- Lifecycle & server: `Run() error`, `Start(ctx) error`, `Shutdown(ctx) error`, `ServeHTTP(w, r)` (`*App` implements `http.Handler` for `httptest`), `BaseURL() string`, `Token() string`, `Config() brisa.Config`.
- Theme: `Theme() brisa.Theme`, `SetTheme(t)` (updates the theme served on future `/brisa/theme.css` requests; does not live-reload open windows automatically).
- Introspection, SDKs & testing: `Dispatch(ctx, command, payload)`, `InspectorSpec()`, `GenerateJSSDK() string`, `GenerateTypeScriptSDK() string`, `RenderInspectorHTML() string`, `RegisterCommand(name, handler, doc)`.

Testing a command without a window:

```go
app := brisa.New(brisa.Config{Store: brisa.StoreOptions{MemoryOnly: true}})
brisa.Bind(app, "greet", handler)
res, _ := app.Dispatch(context.Background(), "greet", map[string]any{"name": "Ada"})
// res.Status, res.Data, res.Error (*ErrorResponse)
```

---

## 12. Styling option A — built-in themes

Set `Config.Theme` and use the shared component classes. The same class names work in every theme; only the look changes.

| Constant | Accepted string aliases | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `brisa.ThemeAdwaita` (default) | `adwaita` | GNOME / Libadwaita |
| `brisa.ThemeUbuntu` | `ubuntu`, `yaru` | Ubuntu Yaru |
| `brisa.ThemePlasma` | `plasma`, `kde`, `breeze` | KDE Breeze |
| `brisa.ThemeMacOS` | `macos`, `darwin`, `aqua`, `mac` | macOS |
| `brisa.ThemeWindows` | `windows`, `win11`, `fluent`, `winui` | Windows 11 Fluent |
| `brisa.ThemeCoke` | `coke`, `coca`, `cocacola`, `coca-cola` | Coke Red (Libadwaita base; `--destructive-*` auto-remapped to orange) |

Light/dark mode is governed by the operating system only. The SDK sets `data-os-theme="light|dark"` and `data-ui-theme="<theme>"` on `<html>` and follows OS changes live. Do NOT build an in-app light/dark toggle, and do not show fake "dark mode" switches.

CSS endpoints: `/brisa/theme.css` (active theme, auto-injected), plus `/brisa/adwaita.css`, `/brisa/ubuntu.css`, `/brisa/plasma.css`, `/brisa/macos.css`, `/brisa/windows.css`, `/brisa/coke.css` (fixed themes; `adwaita.css` is an alias of the active theme). If your HTML already links any of these, Brisa does not inject another one.

### Layout classes

```html
<div class="adw-split-view">                 <!-- 256px sidebar + content grid, full viewport -->
  <aside class="adw-sidebar">
    <div class="adw-sidebar-header">App</div>
    <nav class="adw-nav-list">
      <div class="adw-nav-row active">Home</div>
      <div class="adw-nav-row">Settings</div>
    </nav>
  </aside>
  <section class="adw-content-view">         <!-- optional inner wrapper: .adw-page-container -->
    <header class="adw-toolbar">Title …actions</header>
    <main class="adw-page">                  <!-- or .adw-page.clamped / .adw-page-clamped -->
      <div class="adw-clamp">                <!-- responsive column; modifiers: .tight (680px), .medium (860px), .large (1024px), .wide (1200px), .full (100%), or --clamp-max-width -->
        <div class="adw-group">
          <div class="adw-group-header">
            <div>
              <div class="adw-group-title">Section</div>
              <div class="adw-group-desc">Description</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div class="boxed-list">            <!-- rounded card list -->
            <div class="adw-row activatable">
              <div class="adw-row-prefix">★</div> <!-- 36×36 rounded icon box -->
              <div class="adw-row-text">
                <div class="adw-row-title">Title</div>
                <div class="adw-row-subtitle">Subtitle</div>
              </div>
              <div class="adw-row-suffix">…controls…</div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </main>
  </section>
</div>
```

### Controls & feedback components

```html
<!-- Buttons -->
<button class="gtk-btn">Normal</button>
<button class="gtk-btn suggested-action">Primary</button>
<button class="gtk-btn destructive-action">Delete</button>
<button class="gtk-btn flat">Flat</button>
<button class="gtk-btn circular">✕</button>
<button class="gtk-btn pill">Pill</button>

<!-- Text input (transparent, meant to live inside an .adw-row) -->
<input class="adw-entry-input" placeholder="Type…" />

<!-- Dropdown: upgraded once at DOMContentLoaded into a themed popover menu.
     Keep listening to native "change" and reading select.value. Dynamically inserted <select> elements after load stay native. -->
<select class="gtk-dropdown" id="priority">
  <option value="low">Low</option>
  <option value="high">High</option>
</select>

<!-- Switch (.adw-switch or .gtk-switch) -->
<label class="adw-switch">
  <input type="checkbox" checked>
  <span class="adw-switch-slider"></span>
</label>

<!-- Checkbox / radio (native inputs tinted with the accent color) -->
<label class="adw-check-label"><input type="checkbox"> <span>Auto-save</span></label>
<label class="adw-radio-label"><input type="radio" name="q" value="hi"> <span>High</span></label>

<!-- Slider: the filled part is driven by the --range-progress CSS variable -->
<input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="75" style="--range-progress: 75%;"
       oninput="this.style.setProperty('--range-progress', this.value + '%')">

<!-- Status pills / badges (.gtk-pill or .adw-pill; variants: .accent, .info, .running, .success, .stopped, .error, .destructive) -->
<span class="gtk-pill running"><span class="pulse-dot"></span> Online</span>
<span class="gtk-pill error">Failed</span>

<!-- Preset selector chips -->
<div class="preset-chips">
  <button class="chip-btn active">1h</button>
  <button class="chip-btn">24h</button>
</div>

<!-- Standalone card & empty state -->
<div class="adw-card">Standalone card content</div>
<div class="adw-empty-row">No items yet</div> <!-- or .adw-status-page -->

<!-- Toast overlay (toggle .visible in JS to show/hide) -->
<div id="toast" class="adw-toast-overlay">Saved!</div>
```

Note: all components above are built into `/brisa/theme.css` — do NOT redefine them in custom CSS. A `.hidden` (`display: none !important`) utility class is NOT built in; define it yourself if needed.

### Theme CSS variables you can reuse or override

`--font-sans`, `--control-radius`, `--card-radius`, `--clamp-max-width`, `--window-bg-color`, `--window-fg-color`, `--view-bg-color`, `--view-fg-color`, `--headerbar-bg-color`, `--headerbar-fg-color`, `--headerbar-border-color`, `--sidebar-bg-color`, `--sidebar-fg-color`, `--sidebar-border-color`, `--card-bg-color`, `--card-hover-bg`, `--card-border-color`, `--card-shadow`, `--row-divider-color`, `--dim-label-color`, `--button-bg`, `--button-hover-bg`, `--button-active-bg`, `--nav-active-bg`, `--nav-hover-bg`, `--accent-bg-color`, `--accent-hover-bg`, `--accent-active-bg`, `--accent-fg-color`, `--accent-color`, `--accent-subtle-bg`, `--destructive-bg-color`, `--destructive-hover-bg`, `--destructive-color`, `--success-bg-color`, `--success-color`, `--warning-color`, `--info-bg-color`, `--info-color`, `--focus-ring`, `--popover-bg-color`, `--popover-fg-color`, `--popover-border-color`, `--popover-shadow`, `--popover-hover-bg`, `--popover-active-bg`, `--select-chevron`, `--toast-bg`.

Extending a theme: link your own stylesheet after the injected one and override classes or variables:

```html
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="app.css">  <!-- served from your Assets -->
</head>
```

```css
:root { --accent-bg-color: #9333ea; }
.hidden { display: none !important; }
```

---

## 13. Styling option B — `DisableThemeCSS: true` + your own CSS

Use this when you want full design control (custom design system, Tailwind output, Bootstrap, etc.).

Effects of `DisableThemeCSS: true`:
- No theme `<link>` is injected.
- All theme endpoints (`/brisa/theme.css`, `/brisa/adwaita.css`, `/brisa/ubuntu.css`, …) return 404.
- Everything else keeps working: `/brisa/sdk.js` is still injected, IPC, events, dialogs, store, notifications.
- The SDK still sets `data-os-theme` on `<html>`, so you can follow OS light/dark in your CSS.

### Standalone custom CSS example:

`main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"log"
	"runtime"
	"time"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa"
)

//go:embed ui
var uiAssets embed.FS

type StatsResponse struct {
	Time       string `json:"time"`
	GoVersion  string `json:"goVersion"`
	Goroutines int    `json:"goroutines"`
}

func main() {
	app := brisa.New(brisa.Config{
		AppID:           "com.example.customcss",
		Title:           "Custom CSS Showcase",
		DisableThemeCSS: true,
		Assets:          uiAssets,
		AssetsSubDir:    "ui",
		Window:          brisa.WindowConfig{Width: 820, Height: 560, MinWidth: 620, MinHeight: 420},
	})

	brisa.Bind(app, "stats", func(ctx *brisa.Context, _ brisa.Empty) (StatsResponse, error) {
		return StatsResponse{
			Time:       time.Now().Format("15:04:05"),
			GoVersion:  runtime.Version(),
			Goroutines: runtime.NumGoroutine(),
		}, nil
	}).Summary("Runtime stats")

	log.Fatal(app.Run())
}
```

`ui/index.html`:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Custom CSS</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
  <main class="card">
    <h1>Fully custom design</h1>
    <p>Time: <span id="time">--</span></p>
    <button class="btn" onclick="refresh()">Refresh via IPC</button>
  </main>
  <script>
    async function refresh() {
      const s = await brisa.call.stats();
      document.getElementById("time").textContent = s.time;
    }
    window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", refresh);
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

`ui/style.css` (honoring OS light/dark):

```css
:root { --bg: #ffffff; --fg: #111827; --accent: #6366f1; color-scheme: light dark; }
:root[data-os-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0f172a; --fg: #f8fafc; }
/* fallback before the SDK runs */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-os-theme="light"]) { --bg: #0f172a; --fg: #f8fafc; } }

body { margin: 0; height: 100vh; display: grid; place-items: center;
       background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
.card { padding: 32px; border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.2); }
.btn  { background: var(--accent); color: #fff; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 18px; cursor: pointer; }
```

---

## 14. Frontend frameworks / dev server

- Production: build your frontend (Vite, etc.) into a folder, embed it, point `AssetsSubDir` at it. Brisa injects the SDK into the built `index.html`.
- Development with HMR: set `DevServerURL: "http://localhost:5173"`. Non-`/brisa/*` requests are reverse-proxied to the dev server, and in this mode Brisa does NOT inject anything into the HTML. Add the tags to your dev `index.html` manually:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/brisa/theme.css">   <!-- omit when DisableThemeCSS: true -->
<script src="/brisa/sdk.js"></script>
```

Important: if your HTML already contains `/brisa/sdk.js`, Brisa injects nothing at all (no manifest, no icon, no theme link). Add the theme link yourself in that case.

---

## 15. Built-in HTTP endpoints

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Your `index.html` (with runtime injection) and static assets |
| `/brisa/sdk.js` | JS SDK (contains the session token) |
| `/brisa/rpc` | POST `{command, payload, requestId?}` → `{data, requestId}` or `{error, requestId}`; auth via `X-Brisa-Token` or `?token=` |
| `/brisa/rpc/batch` | POST array of envelopes (`X-Brisa-Token` or `?token=`) |
| `/brisa/events` | SSE stream (`?token=` or `X-Brisa-Token`) |
| `/brisa/schema.json` | Command contract (`InspectorSpec`) |
| `/brisa/types.d.ts` | Generated TypeScript declarations |
| `/brisa/inspector` | IPC Inspector UI (configurable via `InspectorURL`, `"-"` disables) |
| `/brisa/theme.css` and per-theme CSS | Built-in themes (404 when `DisableThemeCSS`) |
| `/brisa/icon.png`, `/favicon.ico`, `/brisa/manifest.json` | App icon and manifest |

Security: the server binds to loopback by default, requires the per-session token on RPC/batch/SSE, and rejects `Host` headers other than loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) or an explicitly configured `Config.Addr` host (DNS rebinding protection). Keep `DisableCSRFToken` false.

The IPC Inspector lists every user command with its input/output schema, lets you execute commands with JSON payloads, and shows the live SSE event stream. Use it to test Go handlers independently of the UI.

---

## 16. Packaging

- macOS `.app` bundle: A standard macOS `.app` structure contains `Contents/MacOS/<binary>`, `Contents/Info.plist` (with `CFBundleIdentifier`, `CFBundleName`, `CFBundleIconFile`, and `NSUserNotificationAlertStyle` set to `alert` or `banner`), and `Contents/Resources/<icon>.icns`. Build with `CGO_ENABLED=1` for native `WKWebView` + Cocoa notifications, and ad-hoc sign the bundle (`codesign --force --deep --sign - "MyApp.app"`) so macOS binds the bundle identity and icon for Notification Center.
- Linux Desktop: At runtime, Brisa automatically writes a `.desktop` entry and icon for `Config.AppID` to `~/.local/share/applications` (and sets `_NET_WM_ICON` on X11) so menus and docks display your app icon. For distribution, build a static binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w"`) or package as an AppImage.

---

## 17. Rules for LLMs generating Brisa code

1. Import only `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa`. Use `brisa.Bind`, `brisa.BindService`, `brisa.BindEndpoint` — there is no `app.Bind`, `app.Handle`, or router API.
2. Handler signature is `func(ctx *brisa.Context, req T) (R, error)`. Use `brisa.Empty` for no input/output.
3. Always put `json:"..."` tags on request/response fields; JS uses those names. Make sure `Config.Icon` is included in your `//go:embed` pattern so packaged builds find it.
4. Only use the validation rules listed in section 6. Never rely on `omitempty` to skip `min`/`len` on empty strings (`omitempty` is a no-op) — use `*string` for optional string fields with `min`/`len`, and use `*bool` / `*int` when `false` or `0` are valid inputs on a `required` field.
5. Do not add `<script src="/brisa/sdk.js">` or theme `<link>` to `index.html` when serving from `Assets` — they are injected. Exception: `DevServerURL` mode.
6. Call commands from JS with `await brisa.call.<group>.<name>(payload)`; handle `brisa.BrisaError` (`e.errors` holds field messages for 422). Always `await` `brisa.window.*`, `brisa.dialog.*`, `brisa.clipboard.*`, and `brisa.store.*` (`store.keys()` returns `{ keys }`, whereas `store.all()` returns the map directly).
7. Light/dark follows the OS. Never generate an in-app dark-mode toggle.
8. With a built-in theme, reuse the built-in classes (`adw-*`, `gtk-*`, `boxed-list`, `adw-switch`, `gtk-pill`, `adw-toast-overlay`, `adw-row-prefix`, `adw-card`, …) instead of re-implementing them; define `.hidden` yourself if needed. With `DisableThemeCSS: true`, write your own CSS.
9. For Go → UI updates, use `app.Emit` / `ctx.Emit` and `brisa.on` in JS; do not poll. Do not rely on `Window.Eval` return values cross-platform (returns `nil` on macOS `WKWebView`).
10. Stop background goroutines with `<-app.Window().Done()` or `<-ctx.Context().Done()`.
11. Return `brisa.NewError(status, "CODE", "message")` for expected failures.
12. Wrap `app.Run()` with `log.Fatal(...)`.
